source.title: Robust Training of Graph Neural Networks via Noise Governance
source.authors: Si-Yi Qian; Haochao Ying; Renjun Hu; Jingbo Zhou; Jin-Tai Chen; D. Chen; Jian Wu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied. No apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own GCN result on graph data bearing on learning clean labels before noisy labels, extending the memorization observation to graph neural networks.
record.gate_note: Figure 2 and its accompanying text report clean and noisy node loss distributions for two graph settings. The paper also reports test accuracies under label noise, but those do not measure the training error or learning order named by V1–V5. Other reported comparisons and ablations concern RTGNN's proposed noise-governance method.
record.test_reason: Figure 2 reports the study's own clean-versus-noisy training-loss comparison for a GCN on graph data, bearing on the early-learning component of V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' interpretation of Figure 2: early clean-label losses are generally lower, motivating loss-based label division. The paper's broader conclusion is that RTGNN improves robustness with scarce, noisy graph labels through noise governance and supplemental supervision.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains graph neural networks for semi-supervised node classification with scarce, corrupted labels; it does not reproduce the original image-classification random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported loss-distribution settings differ by labeled-node fraction (5% versus 10%) and noise type (uniform versus pair).
record.problems: The loss-distribution evidence is figure-only and has no reported uncertainty. It covers two settings on one graph dataset at one stated epoch and does not show the full training trajectory or completely random labels.
record.rows_left_out: None of the study's other reported test-accuracy tables or ablations measure the training-fit, chance-test-error, or learning-order outcomes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Complete random-label fitting, near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true and random labels and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption fractions and steady test-error progression from no corruption to fully random labels.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it impairs true-label generalization.
Training trajectories establishing clean-pattern learning before later noise memorization; completely random-label training.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence consists of loss distributions at one epoch, without numerical summaries or uncertainty. Other accuracy comparisons and mitigation ablations do not establish the training-fit or learning-order outcomes required by the versions.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks fit completely random training labels to zero or near-zero training error, with test error at chance and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training time to fit random versus true labels and how convergence time changes with corruption fraction.
Perfect training fit and test-error progression from no label noise to all labels corrupted.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent random-label fitting or whether their removal harms true-label generalization.
The study measures clean versus noisy label loss distributions in two graph settings; it does not test completely random labels or compare full training trajectories through later memorization.
